name: Fiction serial native (an episodic short story told across a run of ads)
length: 6-episode serial: 6 image ads with 300-600 words each, sequenced 2-3 days apart

shots.visual: Illustration or moody phone photo: a woman at an airport gate touching her necklace. Same style every episode
shots.audio_text: Header text on image: "The Necklace · Episode 1"

shots.visual: Labelled "(A short story. Fiction.)" on line 1
shots.audio_text: Sets up the character and her problem: her late grandmother's chain turned green the night before her sister's wedding. Ends on a cliffhanger.

shots.visual: Same character, new setting each time (sister's house, the beach)
shots.audio_text: The new necklace is just part of her routine: she showers, swims, forgets it's on. Never a pitch.

shots.visual: Tension: someone notices, asks where it's from
shots.audio_text: Dialogue between characters carries the product facts naturally
Resolution + a soft line at the end: "The stack in this story is Louise Carter's. Any 7 for $85."

prompts.prompt: Write a 6-episode fiction serial, 350-450 words per episode, about [character]. Episode 1 opens with a concrete problem; each ends on a cliffhanger; the product appears as a quiet constant (never pitched) until a 1-line note at the end of episode 6. Label each as fiction.
editorial illustration, woman in her 30s at an airport gate touching a thin gold necklace, warm muted palette, gouache texture, consistent character --ar 4:5 --cref [ep1 image] --sref [ep1 image]
Ep1 to a broad audience; Ep2 to people who engaged with Ep1 (post engagement 7d); and so on. Cap frequency at 2 per episode.

qa_checklist: Hook lands in the first 1.5 s (video) or is readable at thumbnail size (static / slide 1).
Removal test: delete the product from the script. If it still makes sense, rewrite so the product is the payoff.
Matches the reference structure (same beat order and length band) before any creative twist.
Uses only real product imagery for the product; AI is for backgrounds, characters or b-roll, and is disclosed where required.
Every claim is on the brand's approved-claims list (PDP); no invented stats, reviews, doctors or customers.
Captions burned in and inside the safe zone; sound-off still understandable.
One clear CTA that matches the landing page offer.
Three hook variants delivered for the same body (test hooks, not whole new ads).
Avoid: Label fiction clearly in every ad; never present it as a true story.
Avoid: Sequencing needs engagement audiences; without them, people see episode 4 first and the story makes no sense.
Avoid: Keep the character consistent (same face and style) or the serial breaks.
inputs: BRAND (name, product, price, offer, audience, proof points, banned claims)
ASSETS (real product photos/video, logo, fonts, colors)
outputs: brands/<brand-slug>.md with 3 concepts in the output schema below
per concept: script/slide copy, shot list, on-screen text, caption, CTA, 3 hook variants, prompts used
